meta: Lots of tasks only need AI to pick one of a few answers: is this email a refund, an exchange or a price question? Decision models do exactly that: take a question and a list, and pick one.
prompt: Reply with exactly one answer from this list

muc.title: Ask for one word, get an essay
muc.text: You only need AI to answer with one word, but it writes a whole paragraph. That's slow, and it costs money.

muc.title: Software only needs one choice
muc.text: Lots of tasks only need AI to pick one of a few ready-made answers. Refund, exchange, or price question?

muc.title: Decision models
muc.text: That's a decision model. You give it a question and a list of answers, and it picks just one, with how sure it is.

muc.title: Jev leads the way
muc.text: In mid-September 2026, a company called TypeSafe launched Jev, a model that does only this job, very fast and very cheap.

muc.title: OpenAI joins in
muc.text: Two weeks later, OpenAI introduced the Decisions API. OpenAI says it picks an answer in about 0.15 seconds, almost ten times faster than a normal reply.

muc.title: Why does it matter?
muc.text: AI agents have to make hundreds of small decisions every day. When each decision is faster, the whole system gets faster and cheaper.

muc.title: Make AI pick just one
muc.text: When you need AI to sort something, give it a list of answers and tell it to reply with exactly one. The reply is short and easy to use, just like how decision models work.
